correctness.rationale: Starting from Pinsky Theorem 2 integral, differentiate s^(l+1)(1-s)^2 W_k(s) and integrate over [0,1] (zero endpoints) to obtain Delta=2 integral_0^1 s^l(1-s)W_k(s)(1-2s^k)ds. Substitute y=s^k and define reflected kernel h_k(y) and r(y)=y^((l-k+2)/k). For y<1/2, exact derivative k y(1-y)(log h_k(y)-log h_k(1-y)) prime = -2+(1-2y) sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(y^(j/k)-(1-y)^(j/k))<-2. Thus h(y)>h(1-y); r nonincreasing for l<=k-2; paired reflected integrand is positive and integrable at endpoints. Independent quadrature and reflected signs for k=2,3,7,21,50 corroborated; all k follow from analytic proof, not finite scans.
